payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
node.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 using the observations and their uncertainty. Return yes only when the edited image establishes that the mug is to the right of the headphones. Return no only when evidence establishes that no requested change has progressed. Return partial when evidence establishes some progress toward moving the mug to the right of the headphones but does not establish completion. Unrelated edits do not count. If the evidence does not establish one of these decisions, return unknown; in particular, an unknown observation must not be treated as a negative. Supporting observations are evidence only and do not independently earn completion credit.
node.binding: Target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.. Reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones..

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is reported to show the mug to the right of the headphones, establishing the requested position. The comparison also reports a change indicating progress toward that move.

dependencies.evidence: In the edited image, the mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.

The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly changed between the source and edited images; the edited image shows a mug on the headphones’ right, indicating progress toward the requested move.

response.content: {"text":"The node overweights the final-state relation and treats any positional change as progress. In the source, the mug is already left of the headphones; in the edit, the rightmost mug is right of them, but the image also shows an additional mug and a blurred mug-shaped remnant at the original location. Do not infer completion from “a mug” being right of the headphones: bind the same source mug across images and assess whether that object was moved, while accounting for duplication/remnant and uncertainty. The trace’s two pass observations do not establish that the requested object was moved or that the edit is complete; distinguish evidence of progress from evidence of fulfillment under the rubric, and lower confidence or return unknown if identity/change cannot be resolved. This is a semantic evidence/criterion issue, not a transport or schema failure."}
